clauses.statement: Immutable Ontology releases and every definition are machine-readable by stable ID and resolvable by current, version, or as-of; when no active current exists, only explicit-version proposed readback is available and current resolution fails explicitly; invalid manifests fail loudly.

story_refs.text: current Ontology version and definitions are readable

clauses.statement: Unknown entity types, relation types, and disallowed relation endpoints are rejected with rule-ID violations before generic Graph persistence.

story_refs.text: invalid relations are rejected before canonical Graph persistence

clauses.statement: Atomic commits prevent Apps without an owner organization and active Decisions without a decider or scope; incomplete DB audits are unverified, never zero violations.

story_refs.text: shared semantic constraints and dry-run audit

clauses.statement: Only an explicit effective supersedes edge resolves a current Decision; unrelated active Decisions remain a conflict with traceable evidence.
Ontology evolution follows SemVer, preserves immutable historical releases and canonical identity, and resolves past facts by recorded version or as-of time.

Info SSOT callers with a valid access context can read current or historical definitions, dry-run, run bounded DB audits, atomically commit aggregates, infer decisions, and analyze impact; without an active current, explicit-version caller snapshots may be validated, inferred, or impact-analyzed, while DB audit and commit remain unavailable.
The MCP Core and Extension type projection remains compatible and existing Graph facts are not automatically modified.
Only an Ontology release approved by the accountable Graph RACI actor and applied with evidence can become canonical active.

story_refs.text: Ontology release governance is linked to RACI

requirements.title: Manifest readback
shall: Immutable releases expose version, previous version, effective date, initial_status proposed, compatibility, migration, and rollback metadata; effective lifecycle status is derived from receipts and the index
Each index release entry stores sha256 metadata for the full bytes of its release file, and the digest is not embedded in that release file
The release index resolves current, explicit version, and as-of requests; absent current returns ONTOLOGY_CURRENT_UNAVAILABLE while explicit version can read a proposed release
Types, relations, constraints, inference rules, and change rules are addressable by stable IDs
An invalid manifest fails loudly at kernel construction

requirements.title: Type and relation vocabulary
shall: Registered types expose meaning and identity boundaries
Registered relations expose endpoint types, direction, cardinality, inverse or symmetry, lifecycle, and provenance
Unknown types, relations, and invalid endpoints produce rule-ID violations

requirements.title: Constraints and dry-run audit
shall: An atomic commit containing an app without an owner org is rejected and rolled back
An active decision without a decider or scope is invalid
Entity, edge, and snapshot validation never persists data
A DB-backed audit proves access scope and pagination completeness
Missing or partial audit input returns unverified rather than zero violations

requirements.title: Decision inference
shall: Explicit effective supersedes edges resolve the current decision
Unrelated active decisions remain a conflict
Inference returns rule ID, ontology version, evidence, as-of time, and explanation

requirements.title: Evolution, history, and impact
shall: Breaking, additive, and patch changes map to SemVer
Rename, merge, and dedup rules preserve canonical identity and provenance
Past facts resolve using recorded versions or immutable as-of releases
Impact reports distinguish evaluated snapshots from unverified input

requirements.title: Info SSOT API
shall: Authenticated callers can read current, explicit-version, and as-of manifests and definitions, with absent current returning 404 ONTOLOGY_CURRENT_UNAVAILABLE
Without active current, explicit-version caller snapshots are allowed for validate, infer, and impact, but versionless calls, DB-backed audit, and graph commit return 503 ONTOLOGY_CURRENT_UNAVAILABLE
Authenticated callers can dry-run validation, run bounded DB audits, infer decisions, and analyze impact
Atomic entity-plus-edge commits reject all semantic violations transactionally, and return 503 ONTOLOGY_CURRENT_UNAVAILABLE when no active current exists

All existing runtime Graph writes reject unknown types, relations, and endpoints before persistence when current is active; without current they preserve legacy behavior and must add guard_status inactive_no_current to every successful response rather than relying only on internal audit

POST /api/info/ontology/publications/authorize derives the actor from authenticated personId and accepts release_version, source_commit_sha, release_digest, decision_id, scope_entity_id, and applier_entity_id

The publication authority endpoint returns a canonical Ed25519 receipt and fails with 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, or 503 for its specified validation, authentication, authority, decision, binding, or dependency failures

requirements.title: Compatibility
shall: MCP Core and Extension type projection remains compatible
Existing specialized relation names are registered
Existing graph facts are not automatically modified
Public IDs, storage types, visibility, aliases, depends_on, ownerless legacy app creation, Companion people writes, and specialized write paths have compatibility fixtures

requirements.title: Release governance
shall: Immutable release files remain initial_status proposed while effective lifecycle status is derived as proposed, approved, active, or retired from receipts and the index
Proposer, decider, and applier identities plus RACI scope and decision evidence are recorded
An unapproved release cannot become current

The sole publisher runs on a clean source commit and validates its SHA, the sha256 of the full release-file bytes, Graph RACI, decision evidence that explicitly approves the version digest and source commit, and applier identity, then stores the digest in the index entry
The verification gate rejects manual current changes, modified or deleted published releases, and reused versions
The PR workflow fetches complete Git history, passes base and head SHAs, and fails closed when the base or source commit object cannot be resolved

A Graph authority endpoint binds the authenticated person principal to the release applier, scope, Accountable RACI, and a decision whose payload explicitly matches the release version source commit SHA and release digest, then returns an Ed25519-signed canonical receipt
The publisher generates the signed receipt, current index, and compatibility pointer view in one operation, and verification rejects receipt or view drift

On a publication PR the publication commit immediately follows the signed source commit and changes only the receipt index and compatibility pointer view; after merge the verifier accepts a merge commit only when that source and direct-child publication pair remain reachable and rejects squash or rebase history that removes the pair
